text: Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, royal house! This judgment is against you, for you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I will discipline them all.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. Ephraim, you have played the whore; Israel is defiled.
Their deeds will not let them return to their God, for a spirit of whoredom is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
Israel's pride testifies against him; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt, and Judah stumbles with them.
With their flocks and their herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.
They have betrayed the LORD, for they have fathered illegitimate children. Now the new moon will devour them along with their fields.
Blow the ram's horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Raise the war cry at Beth Aven: Behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will become a wasteland on the day of punishment. Among the tribes of Israel I declare what is certain.

versions.text: Ephraim will become a wasteland on the day of punishment. Among the tribes of Israel I make known what is certain.
versions.explanation: "I make known what is certain" is stiff for oral reading; "I declare" carries the same sense of authoritative announcement (הוֹדַעְתִּי) with better rhythm.

text: The princes of Judah have become like those who move a boundary stone; on them I will pour out my wrath like water.
Ephraim is oppressed, robbed of justice, because he was determined to go after filth.

versions.text: Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was determined to go after filth.
versions.explanation: "Crushed in judgment" is ambiguous in English and could be misread as God's judgment crushing Ephraim, whereas the Hebrew construct (רְצוּץ מִשְׁפָּט) describes Ephraim being deprived/crushed with respect to justice, i.e. denied its legal right. "Robbed of justice" is clearer and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: So I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent envoys to the great king. But he cannot heal you or cure your wound.

versions.text: When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot heal you or cure your wound.
versions.explanation: "Sent to the great king" lacks an object and sounds clipped when read aloud; "sent envoys" supplies the implied object of וַיִּשְׁלַח without altering the meaning. (A footnote noting that the Hebrew מֶלֶךְ יָרֵב may be read as a proper name, "King Jareb," could also help readers.)

text: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.

versions.text: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue.
versions.explanation: "No one will rescue" leaves the verb without an object, which sounds truncated when read aloud in English; the Hebrew וְאֵין מַצִּיל implies "with none to deliver [them]." Adding "them" completes the clause naturally.

text: I will go and return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will search for me.
